D03.classification: Product regression: unrelated private TREE bytes rewritten by generic failed MAIN-stage fallback
D03.correction: Failed MAIN staging validates independent copies against initial private identity/fingerprint/checkpoint/ref tokens, without writing unrelated private indexes. The original full domain deepEqual assertion is unchanged.

legacyOracle.classification: Actual failure retained: newly guarded protocol was being exercised under a legacy-plan title
legacyOracle.correction: Owned fixture now preserves its original current journal bytes/hash and explicitly writes real schema1 without the new managed guard for legacy cases. Exact official native-replay bytes remain required for that protocol. Two additional managed cases require every original B byte, epoch1, native C detection, flags/stages/OIDs/refs/backups and repeated-journal preservation. No arbitrary stat delta is allowed.

typecheck.qualification: Observed after narrow fallback and test-fixture changes; final global validation has its own receipt.

limitations: These are correctness tests, not activation latency benchmarks.
No external C overwrite or distinct staged-content loss is claimed by the baseline/V6 recapture probes.
Restart after own index restore but before completion can require manual inspection because the restored physical identity is carried only by the current execution.
This correction is limited to managed private add and its checkpoint/recovery; broader historical atomicity boundaries remain explicit.
